findings.issue_text: [High/bug] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:49,107,133,160 — Async legacy writes derive their context from the request context (context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)), so net/http cancels it as soon as the handler returns; the 10s timeout is a ceiling not a floor and legacy Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection goroutines are routinely canceled mid-flight, making mode-3 dual writes unreliable and silently diverging legacy from unified storage. The goroutine needs a detached parent (e.g. context.WithoutCancel(ctx)) before applying the timeout.

[Medium/bug] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:44 — In Create, when Storage.Create fails the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) instead of recordStorageDuration, so the storage failure is never recorded in the storage metric and the legacy metric is polluted with a duration/failure for an operation that never ran.

[Medium/bug] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:128 — Same copy-paste mistake in Update: a storage update failure is recorded via d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) instead of recordStorageDuration.

[Medium/bug] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:105 — In Delete's success path, name (the object name) is passed as the kind metric label (d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, ...)) while the error path and all other methods pass options.Kind, creating unbounded per-object label cardinality in Prometheus and inconsistent labeling within the same method.

[Medium/bug] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:165 — In the DeleteCollection legacy goroutine, the duration is recorded via d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...) instead of d.recordLegacyDuration(...), so legacy delete-collection timings/failures land in the storage metric.

[Medium/bug] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:49-56,107-113,133-140,160-166 — Legacy write errors in the new goroutines are no longer logged (previously each legacy failure was logged with object details); the error is discarded except for a metric counter, making dual-write failures/divergence effectively silent.

[Medium/data] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:125 (Update) — The updateWrapper was removed; legacy storage now receives the raw objInfo and recomputes the updated object from its own old state, so legacy can persist a different object than the one written to unified storage (e.g. JSON/merge patches applied against a diverged or missing legacy base), whereas previously both stores were guaranteed to write the identical object.

[Medium/concurrency] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go — Async legacy writes have no ordering guarantee relative to subsequent requests: a create immediately followed by an update can execute the legacy update before the legacy create (or interleave with other goroutines), leaving the object missing or stale in legacy storage with only a metric to show for it.

[Low/bug] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:96 — In Delete, ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log) should be klog.NewContext(ctx, log); the enriched logger (name/kind/method) is discarded for everything downstream, unlike the other methods.

[Medium/test_gap] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go (all tests) — No test asserts that LegacyStorage methods are invoked, which is the defining behavior of mode 3. Because legacyStoreMock and storageMock share a single mock.Mock, the async legacy calls silently match the storage expectations (e.g. in TestMode3_Delete/TestMode3_DeleteCollection no legacy expectation is set at all), and AssertExpectations is never called, so a regression that stops writing to legacy entirely would go undetected.

[Low/data] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:99-104 (Delete) — Behavior change: on NotFound from unified storage the method now returns immediately without deleting from legacy (the old code still deleted from legacy on NotFound), so objects that exist only in legacy (pre-migration data) are never cleaned up, leaving orphans that can resurface when legacy data is later migrated.

[Low/test_gap] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go, pkg/tests/apis/playlist/playlist_test.go — There is no coverage for legacy-write failure or timeout paths (e.g. verifying that a legacy Create failure doesn't affect the client response), and the new mode-3 integration tests only read back through unified storage, so they cannot detect the async legacy-write cancellation problem in issue 1.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:49,107,133,160 — Async legacy writes derive their context from the request context (context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)), so net/http cancels it as soon as the handler returns; the 10s timeout is a ceiling not a floor and legacy Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection goroutines are routinely canceled mid-flight, making mode-3 dual writes unreliable and silently diverging legacy from unified storage. The goroutine needs a detached parent (e.g. context.WithoutCancel(ctx)) before applying the timeout.

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go the legacy side-effects are executed in goroutines that call `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10*time.Second, ...)` using the *incoming* `ctx` from the request (e.g., Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection). Because that parent context may be canceled as soon as the caller finishes (common for request-scoped contexts), the legacy operation can be canceled immediately despite the 10s timeout, leading to missed legacy writes and divergence while the unified-store operation already succeeded. A detached parent (e.g. `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)`) would be needed to make the async legacy write reliably outlive request cancellation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:44 — In Create, when Storage.Create fails the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) instead of recordStorageDuration, so the storage failure is never recorded in the storage metric and the legacy metric is polluted with a duration/failure for an operation that never ran.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, Create measures `startStorage := time.Now()` then calls `d.Storage.Create(...)`. On error it logs and incorrectly calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ..., startStorage)` even though legacy was not executed and the duration is for the storage attempt. This both fails to record the storage failure in storage metrics and pollutes legacy metrics. (Same pattern also appears in Update’s storage error path: `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ..., startStorage)` after `d.Storage.Update` fails.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:128 — Same copy-paste mistake in Update: a storage update failure is recorded via d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) instead of recordStorageDuration.

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Update`, after `startStorage := time.Now()` the code calls `d.Storage.Update(...)`. On error it executes `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` (using the storage-start timestamp) instead of recording the storage duration (i.e., `recordStorageDuration`). This mismaps a unified-store update failure into the legacy metrics, consistent with the reported copy/paste mistake.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:165 — In the DeleteCollection legacy goroutine, the duration is recorded via d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...) instead of d.recordLegacyDuration(...), so legacy delete-collection timings/failures land in the storage metric.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go within DeleteCollection(), the legacy async goroutine records its duration via `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration(...)`. This misattributes legacy delete-collection latency/errors to the storage metrics, which is a concrete defect visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:49-56,107-113,133-140,160-166 — Legacy write errors in the new goroutines are no longer logged (previously each legacy failure was logged with object details); the error is discarded except for a metric counter, making dual-write failures/divergence effectively silent.

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go, legacy writes (Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection) were changed from synchronous calls that logged errors (e.g., previous Create: `log.WithValues("object", created).Error(err, ...)`, previous Update: `log.Error(errLeg, ...)`, previous Delete: logged non-NotFound legacy errors) to asynchronous goroutines that only call `recordLegacyDuration(...)`/`recordStorageDuration(...)` and never log `err` from the legacy operation. Example: Create now does `go func(){ ... _, errObjectSt := d.Legacy.Create(...); d.recordLegacyDuration(errObjectSt != nil, ...) }()` with no `log.Error`. This makes legacy write failures effectively silent in logs, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:125 (Update) — The updateWrapper was removed; legacy storage now receives the raw objInfo and recomputes the updated object from its own old state, so legacy can persist a different object than the one written to unified storage (e.g. JSON/merge patches applied against a diverged or missing legacy base), whereas previously both stores were guaranteed to write the identical object.

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go, Update was changed from computing the updated object once (via Storage.Get + objInfo.UpdatedObject) and forcing both storages to use the same concrete updated object via updateWrapper, to calling Storage.Update(..., objInfo, ...) and then Legacy.Update(..., objInfo, ...) in a goroutine. This means legacy will re-run objInfo against its own prior state (which may differ from unified storage), so the two backends can persist different resulting objects—an observable correctness/data-consistency regression compared to the previous guarantee in this file.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/concurrency] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go — Async legacy writes have no ordering guarantee relative to subsequent requests: a create immediately followed by an update can execute the legacy update before the legacy create (or interleave with other goroutines), leaving the object missing or stale in legacy storage with only a metric to show for it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes Mode3 legacy writes from synchronous to fire-and-forget goroutines (Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection). E.g., Create() now returns immediately after `d.Storage.Create(...)` and launches `d.Legacy.Create(...)` in a goroutine with a timeout. Update() similarly launches `d.Legacy.Update(...)` asynchronously. There is no per-object sequencing/locking/queueing, so a subsequent request (e.g., Update right after Create on the same name) can start and complete its legacy goroutine before the earlier legacy Create goroutine runs, causing legacy to temporarily (or permanently, on error) miss or have stale state. This is a real correctness/consistency behavior change visible from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go (all tests) — No test asserts that LegacyStorage methods are invoked, which is the defining behavior of mode 3. Because legacyStoreMock and storageMock share a single mock.Mock, the async legacy calls silently match the storage expectations (e.g. in TestMode3_Delete/TestMode3_DeleteCollection no legacy expectation is set at all), and AssertExpectations is never called, so a regression that stops writing to legacy entirely would go undetected.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go the tests use a single shared `m := &mock.Mock{}` for both `legacyStoreMock` and `storageMock`. Expectations are set by method name only (e.g., `m.On("Delete", ...)`), so an async call to `d.Legacy.Delete(...)` in Mode3 (now done in a goroutine in dualwriter_mode3.go) can satisfy the same expectation intended for `d.Storage.Delete(...)`. Additionally, several tests (e.g., TestMode3_Delete/TestMode3_DeleteCollection) set no legacy expectations at all, and none of the tests call `AssertExpectations`, so a regression that stops calling legacy could pass undetected. This is a concrete test-design gap introduced/exposed by the diff, not a runtime bug by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/data] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:99-104 (Delete) — Behavior change: on NotFound from unified storage the method now returns immediately without deleting from legacy (the old code still deleted from legacy on NotFound), so objects that exist only in legacy (pre-migration data) are never cleaned up, leaving orphans that can resurface when legacy data is later migrated.

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go, Delete previously treated a NotFound from d.Storage.Delete specially: it did NOT return and still attempted d.Legacy.Delete (old code checked apierrors.IsNotFound(err) and continued). The new implementation returns immediately on any error from d.Storage.Delete (including NotFound) and only runs the legacy delete in the goroutine on the success path. This is a verifiable behavior change in the diff and can leave legacy-only objects undeleted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go, pkg/tests/apis/playlist/playlist_test.go — There is no coverage for legacy-write failure or timeout paths (e.g. verifying that a legacy Create failure doesn't affect the client response), and the new mode-3 integration tests only read back through unified storage, so they cannot detect the async legacy-write cancellation problem in issue 1.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new async legacy-write behavior in Mode3 (e.g., Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection now spawn `go func()` with `context.WithTimeoutCause(..., 10s, ...)` and do not surface legacy errors to the caller). However, the new unit tests in `dualwriter_mode3_test.go` only assert unified-store results/errs and do not verify the intended contract that legacy failures/timeouts are ignored for the client response (there are no assertions around the goroutine legacy path, timeout/cancellation, or metrics/log side effects). Similarly, the new playlist integration cases enable Mode3, but Mode3 `Get/List` read only from `Storage`, so these tests inherently validate unified storage reads and cannot detect problems in the async legacy-write cancellation path. This is a specific, diff-grounded test coverage gap rather than a proven functional defect in the production code from the diff alone.
